Testimony of Joe Legee, Deputy Director
Maine Emergency Management Agency
BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT
LD 119, "An Act to Include the Declaration of an Emergency by the President of
the United States as a Basis to Allow the Governor to Provide Disaster Relief to Local Governments"
February 26, 2025
Good morning, Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, and distinguished members of the committee on State and Local Government. My name is Joe Legee, and I serve as the Deputy Director for the Maine Emergency Management Agency. |'m here today to testify in support of LD 119, "An Act to lnclude the Declaration of an Emergency by
the President of the United States as a Basis to Allow the Governor to Provide Disaster Relief to Local Governments" .
Maine has experienced a significant rise in the frequency and severity of natural disasters to include the notable storms of December 2023 that caused unprecedented flooding and garnered Maine's first federally funded Individual Assistance program since 2008, and the severe coastal storms of January 2024 that caused millions of dollars in
damage to Maine's infrastructure.
As defined by the Stafford Act, there are two types of disaster declarations granted by the President, at the request of the Governor: Emergency Declarations and Major
Disaster Declarations. Both types authorize the President to provide supplemental
federal disaster assistance to affected Maine communities. This amendment aims to incorporate "Emergency Declarations" into the language of Title 37-B �744 to accurately
reflect the full scope of federal disaster assistance provisions. While Maine has provided disaster relief in past Emergency Declarations, such as the Pre-Landfall Emergency Declaration for Hurricane Lee in 2023, it is not clear under current law that the State has a cost-share obligation in all cases under Emergency Declarations.
Including emergency declarations will synchronize Maine's disaster response framework with federal law, ensuring a cohesive and efficient application of state and federal
resources following disasters.
Thank you for your time and consideration. l welcome any questions you may have.

February 26, 2025

Good morning, Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, and distinguished members
of the committee on State and Local Government. I am Senator Beebe-Center, and I
represent Senate District 12, which is composed of all of Knox County except for the
towns of Washington and Isle Au Haut. I am here today to present LD 119, "An Act to
Include the Declaration of an Emergency by the President of the United States as a Basis to Allow the Governor to Provide Disaster Relief to Local Governments" , on behalf of the Department of Defense, Veterans, and Emergency Management.
This amendment seeks to add "Emergency Declarations" to the language of Title 37-B
�744 to better align State and Federal law regarding disaster recovery.
Maine has faced a notable increase in the frequency and severity of natural disasters.
May we not forget the devastating flooding in December 2023. Then in Januaiy 2024,
back-to-back storms devastated coastal communities, causing millions of dollars in
damage and necessitating extensive recovery efforts.
These events demonstrate the importance of a disaster law that makes available all the
disaster recovery tools being utilized by state and federal authorities.
By passing this amendment, we ensure that State law clearly reflects the requirement
for State disaster support to communities following emergencies and major disasters.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I invite you to direct your questions to the following presenters. Thank you.
